body.heading: The appreciation gap
paragraphs: Think of the last time you felt grateful for someone and said nothing. Now think how often others probably feel the same about you. We run on unspoken appreciation, and everyone is slightly under-fuelled.
People cannot read minds, and 'they know' is usually wrong. The colleague, the sibling, the friend — most have no idea how much they matter to you.

body.heading: Say it specifically
paragraphs: Vague praise evaporates. Specific appreciation sticks: 'The way you handled that call yesterday — calm, clear, kind — I learned something watching you.'
Do not wait for a perfect moment or a special occasion. A message on an ordinary Tuesday carries more weight precisely because nothing prompted it.

description: Most of us feel far more appreciation than we ever say. Closing that gap changes relationships quietly and fast.
